# Changelog

All notable changes to the Genesis Mission documentation repository will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).


## [3.34.68] - 2026-10-10

### Added
- **Processed new reference**: [Brookhaven Lab to Lead $14M AI Project for Nation's Electric Grid Through Genesis Mission](https://news.stonybrook.edu/university/brookhaven-lab-to-lead-14m-ai-project-for-nations-electric-grid-through-genesis-mission/) — ***SBU News — News & Features at Stony Brook University***, the Stony Brook University newsroom (host domain `news.stonybrook.edu`; path `/university/brookhaven-lab-to-lead-14m-ai-project-for-nations-electric-grid-through-genesis-mission/`; page title and link-preview titles printing the variant *BNL to Lead $14M AI Project for Nation's Electric Grid Through Genesis Mission* while the on-page headline and breadcrumb carry the **Brookhaven Lab to Lead …** form, both recorded and neither preferred; breadcrumb **SBU News › Academics › SoMAS** over the category set **Academics · Faculty/Staff · News Highlights · Research · SoMAS · STEM · University**; date line **11 September 2026** with a **“4 min read”** field and a revision dated **14 Sep 2026**; deck **“Project is the eighth Genesis Mission award associated with Stony Brook University”**; lead-image caption crediting **Timothy Kuhn/Brookhaven National Laboratory**; closing tags **AI · Brookhaven National Laboratory · electric grid · faculty · Genesis Mission · research · School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences**; the body closing with **“Read the full story at the Brookhaven National Laboratory website.”** over a link to the already-indexed laboratory release `www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=123136`). Text verified directly at the origin. The register's **fourth** account of the Brookhaven-led grid foundation-model award and the **only** one printed by a partner university's own newsroom, and the **only** record naming **utility and state partners** on it: “Brookhaven National Laboratory has been selected by the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) to lead a **$14.2 million** project to develop a next-generation grid foundation model (**GridFM**), an artificial intelligence (AI) system that can **rapidly simulate scenarios for adding new loads to the electric grid**”, “The award to Brookhaven and its collaborators, including Stony Brook University, was provided through the **Genesis Mission Phase II Request for Application (RFA)**” — the register's only record naming the instrument an **RFA** — “It will support **three years** of research with the goal of building a model that can **simulate one billion scenarios in 24 hours**, aiming to significantly accelerate grid expansion planning with **optimal accuracy, affordability and operational efficiency**”, and “The funding was **announced September 1 at Brookhaven Lab** by DOE's **Assistant Secretary for the Office of Electricity (OE) Catherine Jereza**. **OE is administering the funding** … **$3.9 million** of the total project funds will be allocated to Brookhaven, **with the rest shared among collaborating institutions**”. *Roster (page wording)*: “Collaborators on the GridFM Genesis Mission Phase II project include **Stony Brook University**, the **New York Power Authority**, the **Long Island Power Authority**, **National Grid** and the **New York State Energy Research and Development Authority (NYSERDA)**. **The GridFM initiative is a community project spanning industry, academia and government, with contributions from more than 150 organizations.**”, the utilities providing “**operational data and system experience**”, researchers and technology providers “**AI expertise and computing resources**”. *Statements (verbatim)*: **Hendrik Hamann** — here “**Principal Investigator**”, Brookhaven's chief AI scientist for Innovation, Science, and Security and a Stony Brook **School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences** professor — “AI is often seen as a growing burden on the electric grid, but through the Genesis Mission we have an opportunity to **turn that challenge into an advantage** … we can **accelerate planning, improve operations and efficiency**, and help build a more affordable, resilient energy system”; Laboratory Director **John Hill** — “This award reflects DOE's confidence in Brookhaven Lab to bring together science, artificial intelligence,and strong partnerships to address challenges of national importance” (comma splice reproduced **as printed**) and “we need **new approaches to strengthen, expand and efficiently operate the nation's electric grid**”; **Catherine Jereza**'s statement reproduced from the office's release, printing “**utilities-enhanced AI tools**” where the office's copy reads *utilities enhanced AI tools*. *Campus staffing (page wording)*: “**Yue Zhao**, an associate professor of electrical and computer engineering at Stony Brook, is collaborating with Hamann on the GridFM initiative”; a **separate** Phase II award through “**Yixin “Berry” Wen**, an assistant professor in **SoMAS** and the **Institute for Advanced Computational Science** … developing **AI methods to produce hyperlocal precipitation, runoff and flood-risk information for U.S. energy systems**” (previously at the **University of Florida**); and “**Six Stony Brook researchers were among the initial Genesis Mission Phase II awards announced in July**”. *Provenance recorded with the entry*: a **university newsroom republication of the laboratory's announcement, not an award instrument** — no award number, DOE obligation, cost-share basis, phase budget, selection ratio or per-partner amount beyond the laboratory's **$3.9 million**; the value held at **$14.2 million** against the **DOE Office of Electricity's $11.5 million**, which the page never prints, the variance left **unreconciled**; a **fourth, non-identical collaborator roster**, with **NYPA / LIPA / National Grid / NYSERDA** named nowhere else and the elsewhere-named **National Laboratory of the Rockies / MIT / IBM Research / Argonne / AWS / Hydro-Québec** absent, no roster treated as complete; **no** named partner tied to the office's **two utility-partner deployments**, which remain unidentified; **Hamann** as PI held **beside** the *Illinois iSchool*'s **He / Tong** attribution and the laboratory's directorship framing; the **“eighth Genesis Mission award”** and **“six … researchers”** tallies held **beside**, not merged with, the **five**-award *Stony Brook Matters* itemisation; every capability verb prospective, with **no benchmark, baseline, codebase, model architecture or validation case**; **“more than 150 organizations”** describing the whole GridFM community initiative rather than this award; **National Grid** carried exactly as printed with **no legal-entity determination**; and the **University of Florida** named only as Wen's prior institution and **not** registered.
- **Enriched paper sections**: `README.md` §3.2 *National Laboratories* — a new closing sub-bullet **GridFM Utility, Community-Project & Campus-Roster Record (Stony Brook University · *SBU News*, 11 Sep 2026)** appended at the bottom of the **Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL)** profile, carrying the award, RFA, dating, administering-office, **$3.9 million** share, four-New-York-partner roster, **more-than-150-organizations** community-project and quotation blocks plus the attribution and roster notes; §3.3 *University Research Partners* — a new entry **Stony Brook University · *SBU News* · Brookhaven-Led GridFM Phase II Partner Record (11 September 2026)** appended at the bottom of the *Grid Decarbonization, Climate & Geospatial AI* block with five sub-bullets (**Award & Role**; **Named Utility & State Partners**; **Campus Team & a Second Phase II Award**; **Investigator Statements & Positioning**; **Cross-Source Reconciliation & Provenance**, itemising the five surviving disagreements **(a) award value $14.2M-vs-$11.5M**, **(b) partner roster**, **(c) leadership attribution**, **(d) the campus tally**, **(e) the unidentified demonstration utilities**); §3.4 *Federal Agencies & Policy Bodies* — a new sub-bullet **University-Side Corroboration of the Announcement Event (Stony Brook University, 11 Sep 2026)** appended at the bottom of the **DOE Office of Electricity (OE)** entry, recording what the campus edition independently corroborates (the **1 Sep 2026** Brookhaven announcement, **OE as administering office**, the project title, the three-year and billion-scenario framing, the Assistant Secretary's statement) and what it withholds (the office's **$11.5 million**, its **>10,000×** and **>1,000×** multipliers, and the identity of the two deployment utilities). Jeremy Leong** — **„The AMC has quickly become a space where people feel energized to explore, experiment and build … Our first year has been defined by collaboration and real teamwork that accelerates discovery and brings new ideas to life. We are just getting started."** —, the regional passage **„Its location on the University of South Carolina Aiken campus affords unique opportunities for college and high school students to explore STEM careers."**, and the lead image credit carrying the same site-visit scene as the syndicated copy: **Assistant Secretary of Environmental Management Tim Walsh** visiting with Director **Johney Green** at the AMC „prior to SRNL's employee celebration of the AMC's one-year anniversary". **Link-emission artifact**: **every** in-body outbound link is emitted as a **Microsoft SafeLinks** wrap (`gcc02.safelinks.protection.outlook.com`) around a **GovDelivery** click-tracking redirect (`links-1.govdelivery.com/CL0/…`), one wrapper token embedding an **`@em.doe.gov`** staff address; Jul 2026** `dateModified` standing against a **22 Jun 2026** printed date line (the page therefore carries three mutually inconsistent date signals and no printed modification line); and an **"Estimated Read Time" field rendered with no number at all**. **Genesis statements, verbatim**: "The U.S. is entering a decisive moment in the global race for artificial intelligence leadership. For the Department of Energy's Office of Environmental Management — responsible for one of the world's largest and most complex environmental cleanup missions, AI is not a far-off idea, it is a practical and powerful tool we can use right now to deliver faster, safer, and more cost-effective progress."; "Recent directives from President Trump are mobilizing a historic, government-wide effort to strengthen America's AI leadership with an urgency comparable to previous great national efforts like the Manhattan Project. **The Department of Energy's Genesis Mission stands as this generation's great scientific endeavor.**"; and "By bringing together America's national laboratories, leading AI companies, advanced data infrastructure and decades of scientific datasets, Genesis facilitates significant opportunities for innovation across federal missions. This approach aims to enhance efficiency, cost-effectiveness and responsiveness by **supporting human expertise rather than substituting it**." **The six application lines the office names** (all quoted verbatim in the papers): tank-waste analytics — "Across the environmental management tank waste mission, AI and machine learning are accelerating analyses of decades of data, reducing uncertainty and helping move waste out of at-risk conditions more quickly", plus "AI and machine learning tools that help monitor and predict the formation of flammable gases in the storage and processing of tank waste"; Savannah River process digital twins — "digital twins and neural-network models are replicating chemical processing facilities to identify potential improvements to filter cleaning and operational strategies, reducing downtime and mitigating implementation risks", with "Similar strategies … being considered at Hanford to enhance the final waste form composition and inform processing parameters, flowsheet chemistry, and final designs of the treatment facilities"; machine-learning-driven robotics in nuclear materials reprocessing, so that "complex handling tasks [are] performed remotely in high-dose environments" and "chemical separation of fissile materials is conducted with a degree of consistency and safety that exceeds manual operations", with "modern robotic platforms equipped with radiation-hardened sensors … performing real-time monitoring and maintenance, extending the operational lifespan of reprocessing facilities"; Text verified directly at the origin. **Departmental award roll-up (page wording)**: "**Six physics faculty** from CU Boulder are leading or contributing to new projects awarded **more than $1.6 million** in highly competitive U.S. Department of Energy Genesis Mission grants, the agency announced on **July 22**. Nationwide, only **278 phase-one projects** were funded out of **over 5,000 proposals.**" **Role assignment exactly as printed**: "**Yuan Shi** and **Keith Ulmer** are principal investigators on their respective projects, **Dennis Perepelitsa** is a co-principal investigator on **two** projects, **Jamie Nagle** is a co-principal investigator on another, and **Xun Gao** and **Scott Parker** are collaborators on the project led by Shi" — six physics faculty across **four** projects. **Departmental framing of the Mission**: "The Genesis Mission is a historic national initiative led by the U.S. Department of Energy, which is building the world's most powerful integrated science discovery platform. By uniting government, industry, academia, and philanthropy, it is accelerating breakthroughs in energy, scientific discovery, and national security through a new platform that combines **AI, supercomputing, quantum systems, and advanced scientific instruments.**" **Departmental assessment**: "Having six CU Physics faculty involved across four Genesis Mission projects is incredibly impressive," says **Tobin Munsat, professor and chair of physics**; "This reflects the broad strength of our department and demonstrates how our faculty are leading the way in putting AI and quantum technologies to work on some of the most challenging questions in fundamental science." **Project 1 — *AI for analyzing particle collisions at the Large Hadron Collider***: "Ulmer, with collaborators from the **University of California San Diego**, **Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory** and **Johns Hopkins University**, will use AI to analyze largely untapped datasets of particle collisions from the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN"; "Each day, the LHC produces about **4,000 petabytes, or 4 billion gigabytes**, of particle collision data", and "because of the enormous amount of data, current analyses are limited to **roughly one in every 10,000 particle collisions, leaving potential anomalies undetected**"; "Called the **AI-Inclusive Discovery of Anomalies in Scouting (AIDA-Scout)**, the system will analyze data **in real time**, **automatically adjust to changing detector conditions**, and **find anomalies** in collision data that could lead to new scientific discoveries", built "by combining high-energy physics expertise, data science, and industry AI methods". **Project 2 — *Using quantum computing technologies and AI to simulate plasma for fusion pilot plants***: "Shi is leading a project to generate plasma simulations needed for fusion pilot plants. Collaborators on the project include **Gao and Parker**, as well as colleagues from **Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory** and **Infleqtion**"; "Even today's most powerful supercomputers cannot produce certain plasma simulations essential for developing fusion pilot plants", so the team "will develop new computational methods combining **quantum computing, quantum machine learning, and AI**"; Shi: "This project seeks to **prepare the fusion community for the coming generation of quantum computers** by creating algorithms and software that can take advantage of quantum hardware as it matures … The resulting capabilities could significantly accelerate plasma simulations, supporting advances in fusion energy science and scientific computing." **Project 3 — *AI for understanding quark-gluon plasma***: "A project led by **Baruch College, City University of New York** involves CU Boulder physics faculty **Jamie Nagle** and **Dennis Perepelitsa** as **co-principal investigators**. The project's leadership team includes **Yeonju Go**, a former postdoctoral researcher in CU Boulder's experimental nuclear physics group"; the target is "quark-gluon plasma, a phase of matter which only existed **microseconds after the Big Bang at temperatures exceeding two trillion Kelvin**", recreated "at Brookhaven National Laboratory … by colliding **gold nuclei** together at nearly the speed of light" and analysed by "the **sPHENIX** detector, which acts as a giant camera, capturing **approximately 15,000 particle collisions each second**"; the two-high-energy-quark scattering images are separated and analysed "by using an **unsupervised AI framework known as cycle-consistent generative learning**" — Nagle: "We know how quarks scatter at high energy, but we want to understand how they scatter when they're **inside the plasma**."; the accompanying photograph is captioned "Some of the **final collisions** captured by the sPHENIX detector at the **Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider**, a nuclear physics research facility at Brookhaven National Laboratory. (Image Credit: **Brookhaven National Laboratory**)". **Project 4 — *AI for enhancing the foundation model for nuclear and particle physics***: "Dennis Perepelitsa is a co-principal investigator on a project led by colleagues at **Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory** aimed at enhancing the **Foundation Model for Nuclear and Particle Physics (FM4NPP)**, a large-scale AI model built to extract scientific insights **directly from raw detector data**"; "Foundation models go beyond the more commonly known large language models (LLMs) by being able to perform a variety of tasks"; the award "will extend the current FM4NPP, which only includes information from **one sPHENIX detector subsystem**, to include a **variety of other detectors**, making the model **truly multi-modal** and enhancing the capability of the detector for quark-gluon plasma measurements", and "ultimately, the FM4NPP effort is **envisioned as a multi-institution consortium between national labs, universities, and industry** to accelerate scientific discovery in a broad set of nuclear and particle physics datasets"; Perepelitsa: "In modern collider detectors, physics processes leave signatures in **multiple subsystems at once**, and a comprehensive picture is needed for the highest scientific sensitivity. The foundation model is based on similar principles as commercial LLMs, which is that **with enough data and scale, it can make connections beyond the existing non-AI approaches.**" *Provenance note*: a **departmental companion record** to the university-wide release already carried in this register — it announces **no** new selection, no DOE obligation and no project outside the 22 July 2026 Phase I cohort, and its **"more than $1.6 million"** is the department's own aggregate for the Physics share; that figure is arithmetically consistent with the four physics-department awards itemised in the university release (**$729,800** Shi + **$659,157** Ulmer + **$161,000** Nagle/Perepelitsa on the Baruch College-led project + **$127,000** Perepelitsa on the LLNL-led FM4NPP project = **$1,676,957**), a summation that is this paper's own cross-source arithmetic and is stated by neither CU Boulder page nor DOE; the department counts **four projects / six physics faculty** where the university-wide release counts **six grants / more than $2.4 million** because the **David Bortz** fusion-plasma-control and **Zhi Li** water/flood-prediction awards sit outside the Physics department; **Baruch College (CUNY)**, the **LLNL-led FM4NPP** consortium and the **sPHENIX/RHIC** instrumentation are named within this register **only** by this single departmental page — no independent college, project, model-card, laboratory or facility page was fetched — and the **~15,000-collisions-per-second** figure accompanies a caption about "some of the **final** collisions", so it is carried as the department's description of the instrument and not as evidence of current running conditions. "a team of about **30 members** of the ArtIMis project participated in a hackathon under the direction of **Earl Lawrence**, the **National Nuclear Security Administration's models pillar lead for the Genesis Mission** — a Department of Energy-wide AI effort — and a **senior scientist in the Computing and Artificial Intelligence Division Office**"; co-PI **Nathan DeBardeleben** (senior research scientist) likens its use "to a mentor giving a mentee a problem to solve" — "It works toward a solution and then finally stops when it thinks it has met your criteria … **You can pick up the pieces whenever you want with URSA at these checkpoints and steer it back on course.**" **Foundation-model integration**: participants "integrated ArtIMis products known as '**scientific foundation models**' into URSA. ## [3.34.41] - 2026-10-09

### Added
- **Processed new reference**: [What Sandians are saying about the future of AI at work](https://www.sandia.gov/labnews/2026/02/12/what-sandians-are-saying-about-the-future-of-ai-at-work/) — the **Sandia National Laboratories** *Lab News* staff roundtable on artificial intelligence in the workplace (host domain `www.sandia.gov`; page title *What Sandians are saying about the future of AI at work – LabNews*; dated **12 February 2026**; attributed on the page to **Troy Rummler**, whose on-page *Recent articles* shelf also lists *Tight light helps quantum sensing get ready for the field*, *In the Mountain West, a quantum computing collaboration announces major results* and *Sandia selected to lead six Genesis Mission projects, partner on 17 others*; both on-page photographs credited to **Bret Latter**). Text verified directly at the origin. *URL note: the entry is registered under the site's own canonical slash-date address, matching the sibling Lab News records already carried for the laboratory; the dash-date address carried in the intake queue resolves to the identical page.* **Opening framing (feature wording)**: Energy Secretary **Chris Wright**, visiting New Mexico "last February", "described artificial intelligence as having the same urgency as the Manhattan Project", and "in November, President Trump signed an executive order launching DOE's Genesis Mission to advance the technology for government work"; while "The White House's commitment is clear", the feature's stated question is "how much of this AI fervor has made its way through the rank and file of the Labs?" **Internal workforce poll (as printed)**: "Sandia polled members of its workforce in August with a single question, asking their feelings about using the technology at work. **An astounding 8,573 people responded, 79% saying they saw at least some benefit to AI.** *The Lab News* asked AI leaders from around the Labs for their reactions to the poll results, and about trends, opportunities and challenges they see surrounding AI in our workplace"; the page publishes no sampling methodology, question wording or margin of error, so the figures are carried as the laboratory's own reporting of a single-question staff poll rather than an independently administered survey. **Tina Nenoff** (Sandia Fellow; Labs AI strategy lead) attributes the response to "positive reinforcement from leadership at all levels to the staff" and to "[a]dding **top cover from management to staff** for the incorporation of AI into mission work", "as is covering risks that might arise for bringing this new technology into the workflow"; states that "Sandia's leadership is fully committed to incorporating AI into the Sandia enterprise in a safe and secure manner", and that **to help teams scale up AI workflows into mission-critical work, Sandia's Senior Leadership Team has made an AI investment area in FY 26** working "toward a **minimum viable capability**" that includes **Sandia's inclusion into the Venado/OpenAI collaboration venture at LANL**, the **Sandia toolkit** and **SandiaAI Chat**; she further names **Sandia's AI Board of Directors** together with "our leadership teams for the **DOE-sponsored Genesis work** and the **NNSA-sponsored AI for National Security program**" as introducing "AI research and development into mission work through **demonstration projects, use cases and lighthouse problems**, especially difficult tasks that fold back into the Genesis Mission", and expects Sandia's designation as "the premier engineering lab for national security" to be "unquestioned" "in just a couple of years, when we've fully incorporated AI into our mission workflow". **Dan Turner** (AI for Nuclear Deterrence lead) supplies the internal counterweight: the more diagnostic statistic "would be the number of people who could testify to transformational impacts from AI"; "I've seen the initial excitement over what AI could do subside as people realize how hard it is to achieve transformational results. **Many pilot projects are showing progress, but they struggle to scale when the pilot is over.** What we need are sustained efforts that can overcome these challenges by leveraging the tools we have in creative and effective ways." He names the Genesis Mission — "the large DOE investment in AI" — as Sandia's route through that barrier because "**This will provide the AI platform and models we need to scale to an enterprise AI capability**", and filters candidate work by return on investment: "it all boils down to focusing on what will lead to the highest return on investment… the efforts that will win the day will be those that pay for themselves and then some". **Gregory Butler** (Facilities and Infrastructure AI champion) records an operational deployment outside research: "in Facilities, we utilize a **containerized chatbot with a visual language model to extract and analyze fire protection data from scanned forms**, which helps to eliminate a considerable amount of administrative time", with wider chatbot use planned "as **retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG**, tools improve", and a problem-first adoption rule — "What is the problem we are trying to solve?" — against "starting with the cool AI tool and just trying to think of where we can use it". **Siva Rajamanickam** (**BANYAN Generative AI Institute**) calls himself "an AI optimist" who is "not surprised by the 79% number. I would like that number to be 100%", names the research agenda as "learning how to integrate **AI agents** with our modeling and simulation tools, experimental capabilities, data sets, prototyping and manufacturing capabilities", and reports that "**We are also starting to explore federated training and inference approaches at the tri-labs and at the complex level. We are working toward building an AI platform that will become a foundation to transform the future of science and security**"; his near-term picture is a designer served by "a suite of customized AI agents" that "help create new questions, generate hypotheses, generate a set of designs that match the hypotheses, evaluate those designs and present our designers with multiple choices over a weekend" — "This might sound like Iron Man and JARVIS, but it is not too far-fetched." **On-page captions**: *AUDIBLY IMPRESSIVE* shows **Danny Gomez**, "a former applied machine intelligence expert at Sandia", coaching Yucca Middle School teacher **Laura DeBusk** through **JARVIS**, "a virtual reality environment that uses AI to answer users' questions with real-time, audible answers in natural language"; *WORK BUDDIES* shows "[s]ingle-board computers [running] a neural-network AI developed at Sandia". Quoted wording, job titles, dates and poll figures are Sandia's own; this is a laboratory staff publication, so the four contributions are individually attributed staff perspectives, and the FY 26 AI investment area, minimum-viable-capability scope, tri-lab federated-training work and "premier engineering lab" claim are internal institutional statements rather than DOE announcements.
- **Enriched paper sections**: `README.md` §3.2 *National Laboratories* — the **Sandia National Laboratories (SNL)** profile received two new sub-entries: *Workforce AI Adoption & FY 26 Enterprise Capability Build-Out (Sandia Lab News, 12 February 2026)* (the single-question August staff poll with its **8,573 responses / 79% "at least some benefit to AI"**, the "top cover from management" and U.S. Department of Energy's Brookhaven National Laboratory, **effective May 21**"; Hill is "a longtime employee at Brookhaven Lab" who "has served as **interim lab director since September 2025**"; "BSA's board of directors selected Hill **after a competitive international search**" and "Hill will also serve as **BSA's president**". **Management-and-operating provenance**: "BSA — a partnership DOE Under Secretary for Science **Darío Gil** calls the leadership change critical to "advancing the groundbreaking EIC, **which will incorporate AI from the ground up**". **Institutional metrics as printed**: Hill will "expand capabilities at **NSLS-II**", "a DOE Office of Science user facility"; the Lab "will celebrate its **80th anniversary in 2027**" and "is home to **seven Nobel Prize-winning discoveries**". **Career record as printed**: Physics Department postdoc from **1992**; **deputy director for science and technology 2023–2025**; **director of NSLS-II 2015–2023**; deputy associate laboratory director for energy and photon sciences **2013–2023**; director of NSLS-II's Experimental Facilities Division **2006–2008**; leader of the **X-ray Scattering Group 2001–2013**; bachelor's degree in physics, **Imperial College in London**; resident of Stony Brook, New York. **Recorded with provenance caveats**: the **Grid AI Foundation Office** listed in the newsroom site navigation under the Lab's *Innovation, Science, and Security* directorate is flagged as a navigation element rather than article text, and the page's *Other Articles* shelf — *Energy Department Announces New Genesis Mission Awards to Advance Super Intelligence for Science* and *Complete List of Brookhaven Lab Genesis Mission Phase II Projects* (both **8 October 2026**), *Luca Cultrera Leads by Learning* (**8 October 2026**), *Student Engineer Designs Magnet Stands for Next-Gen Collider* (**5 October 2026**), *Building Smart Tools — and Career Skills — at Brookhaven Lab* (**2 October 2026**) — is recorded as titles printed on the page, not independently re-verified in this round. the full article was read through the working canonical form of the same story, [news.gatech.edu/news/2026/08/03/georgia-tech-lead-national-cloud-laboratory-advanced-manufacturing-and-materials](https://news.gatech.edu/news/2026/08/03/georgia-tech-lead-national-cloud-laboratory-advanced-manufacturing-and-materials), and the canonical URL is carried alongside the queued address in every tracker.* **Award & network**: the cloud lab is **"supported by $18.1 million from the National Science Foundation (NSF)"** and is part of "a broader effort to build a national network of **20 AI-enabled cloud laboratories**" whose members "are designed to work together, eventually allowing researchers to combine capabilities and workflows across the network", a "new research ecosystem" connecting "advanced scientific infrastructure with expertise across the country" — placing the Georgia Tech node beside the already-documented Penn State **LATTICE**, Virginia Tech semiconductor and Carnegie Mellon **AI Science Foundry** nodes of the **NSF PCL Testbed** family. **Facility base**: built upon the **Advanced Manufacturing Pilot Facility (AMPF)**, "a core facility of the **Georgia Tech Manufacturing Institute (GTMI)**", a mixed-use site where "both industry and academic partners can discover new materials and do manufacturing research"; remote researchers "direct work remotely, refine experiments based on results and AI recommendations, and tap into advanced manufacturing capabilities without spending weeks on-site" — "the cloud lab will bring the facility to the researcher". **Automation scope**: AMPF is "approaching autonomous workflow capabilities across about **38 pieces of equipment**" and the project aims to extend automated and autonomous workflows to **more than 100 of AMPF's 160 pieces of equipment**, while uniting **materials discovery, manufacturing, testing and scale-up** in a single research environment. **Orchestration layer**: robots operate machines and move materials between stations to execute remotely requested workflows; AI decides "which machines and robots are needed for each task" and manages their movement across the facility; **AI agents** translate high-level researcher "recipes" into detailed workflows and coordinate experiments, simulations and data flows; and **digital twins** — virtual models of the facility — plan, monitor and improve runs, the system being "designed to learn from each run, improving how machines are tuned and how future workflows are scheduled" (**Pascal Van Hentenryck**, director of the **NSF AI Institute for Advances in Optimization** and the A. Russell Chandler III Chair in the H. Milton Stewart School of Industrial and Systems Engineering, whose recipe/stove analogy frames the interaction). **Distributed software & data partners**: **Duke University**'s **Automatic FLOW for Materials Discovery** platform (led by professor **Stefano Curtarolo**) connects computational discovery with physical experimentation; **Contextualize** (founder and CEO **Branden Kappes**) provides "the data platform that seamlessly connects researchers, instruments, data, and IT systems across the distributed network"; **Tech AI** contributes "as part of the broader research team". **Named leadership & quotations**: executive vice president for Research **Tim Lieuwen** ("By making advanced manufacturing and AI-driven experimentation accessible from anywhere, we are accelerating the discovery of critical new materials and shaping the future of U.S. innovation"; "Georgia Tech is proud to provide the world-class infrastructure to help meet this national need and strengthen our research partnerships"); GTMI associate director **Aaron Stebner** (Eugene C. Gwaltney Jr. Chair; James R. and Sarah R. Borders Faculty Fellow; professor in the School of Materials Science and Engineering and the George W. Woodruff School of Mechanical Engineering) on the "ask a question → AI-recommended work → robotic execution → results back" model, on lowering cost and access barriers, and on the six-year build-out ("we are six years into this effort, and we're already at a place I thought would take us 20 years to reach"); and GTMI executive director **Tom Kurfess** (Agustin A. Ramirez/HUSCO International Distinguished Chair in Fluid Power Systems in ME) on giving "industry partners and manufacturers the ability to evaluate new ideas before they commit to large-scale deployment", shortening development cycles and enabling partners "to innovate at the speed of thought". **Access targets & industrial function**: **more than 400 users from 150 academic, industry, and government institutions, with more than half participating remotely**, and de-risking of emerging technologies outside live production lines, since "companies can be reluctant to interrupt working production lines to test unproven technologies, while startups and academic researchers often lack access to industrial-scale facilities". *Provenance note: this is an **NSF** Programmable Cloud Laboratory award, **not** a DOE Genesis Mission award; the page carries no DOE/Genesis narrative of its own — its only Genesis element is the on-page related-items card to the already-indexed Georgia Tech Genesis Mission release — and is registered because Georgia Tech is a Genesis Mission participant with **seven** projects involving its researchers, because AI-driven autonomous laboratories are one of the Mission's national science and technology challenges, and because the page is the primary source for the autonomous-experimentation substrate (AMPF/GTMI) referenced by the papers' §2.3C/§2.4C closed-loop laboratory layer. Rubin Observatory** will generate about **7 million science alerts per night** during the **Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST)** and up to **30 petabytes** across its **10-year** survey, "more than any other optical astronomical survey to date", while **LCLS** X-ray pulses arriving at **up to a million times per second** produce **up to 40 terabytes of data in as much time**, unprocessed accumulating to "zettabytes (1 billion terabytes) of data each year" — calibrated against the **100 zettabytes** the world's **30 billion cloud-connected smart devices** produce today; **Lisa Bonetti** (SLAC associate lab director for Technology Innovation and head of the **Integrated Scientific and Data-Intensive Computing (ISDCI)** Initiative) expects the enormous datasets to "feed the AI revolution and lead to future technologies with broad societal benefits". **Platform layer**: the **SLAC Shared Science Data Facility (S3DF)** — hub for data from **more than two dozen DOE Office of Science projects** and home of the Rubin Observatory's **U.S. Data Facility** — is "a key partner in the **American Science Cloud (AmSC)**", the hardware-and-software infrastructure on which partners "make data AI-ready, train AI models, search for and use previously developed AI models, and analyze data", and it supports the **SLAC Sandbox for Streaming AI (S3AI)** interface to AmSC and the broader DOE ecosystem for evaluating and benchmarking "unique combinations of hardware and trained AI models to continuously process data at ultrahigh rates in real or near-real time"; - **Processed new reference**: [Stony Brook University Researchers Chosen for Landmark DOE Genesis Mission AI-for-Science Awards](https://sbmatters.stonybrook.edu/stony-brook-university-researchers-chosen-for-landmark-doe-genesis-mission-ai-for-science-awards/) — *Stony Brook Matters — News for Alumni & Friends*, the **Office of Advancement** publication of **Stony Brook University** (host domain `sbmatters.stonybrook.edu`, page title *Stony Brook University Researchers Chosen for Landmark DOE Genesis Mission AI-for-Science Awards - Stony Brook Matters*, WordPress category *Excellence*, dated **24 July 2026**, deck *"More than $2.4M will support collaborations with Brookhaven National Lab and other institutions to address complex science and technology challenges"*). Content retrieved and verified in this round (the origin refuses automated retrieval, so the text was read from a cached copy of the same URL, taken with the page's published timestamp **2026-07-24T12:00:00-04:00**). Distinct from the two already-indexed `news.stonybrook.edu` press-release copies of the same announcement, this is the only Stony Brook source that itemizes all **five inaugural Genesis Mission awards** individually with amounts and partner rosters. **Awards**: five inaugural awards bringing **more than $2.41 million** in combined project funding, announced **22 July 2026** at the **Genesis Mission Summit** at the **Capital Hilton** in Washington, D.C., where leaders of DOE, Congress, the national laboratories, universities and industry gathered to launch the national initiative, described as connecting **advanced computing systems, experimental facilities, AI capabilities and scientific datasets** to address **21 national science and technology challenges**; Stony Brook was **among just 278 awardees selected from more than 5,000 applications**. **Summit keynote**: **Hendrik Hamann** (chief AI scientist at Brookhaven National Laboratory for Innovation, Science, and Security; professor at Stony Brook's **School of Marine and Atmospheric Sciences**) was one of **five** people delivering Genesis Mission technical keynotes, on **"How AI Is Transforming the Electrical Grid."** **Three university-led projects (nearly $1.68 million directly to Stony Brook; collaborations with Brookhaven, Argonne and Sandia National Laboratories, Indiana University and GE Vernova)**: **Jan C. Bernauer** (Physics and Astronomy), *Foundation Models for Transferable Particle Tracking in Nuclear Physics*, with **BNL** and **Argonne** — foundation models learning directly from raw particle-detector data across multiple nuclear-physics experiments and detector technologies, improving particle tracking while reducing the need for a separate data-analysis system per experiment; **Emre Salman** (Electrical and Computer Engineering), *AI-Driven Autonomous and Self-Healing Readout Electronics for Radiation-Tolerant HEP Detectors*, with **BNL** and **Indiana University** (**Total Amount to Stony Brook and National Lab Partners: $700,000**) — AI-enabled resilience of detector readout chips in radiation-intensive environments via monitoring, identification of radiation-induced disruptions and carefully controlled corrections (Salman, quoted: the award "will enable our multidisciplinary team to establish the experimental and technological foundation for a new generation of reliable, autonomous microelectronics"); **Shikui Chen** (Mechanical Engineering), *Geometry-Informed AI for Accelerated Multiphysics Co-Design of Wide-Bandgap Power Modules*, with **Sandia** and **GE Vernova** (**Total Amount to Stony Brook and National Lab Partners: $723,076**) — rapid design evaluation, cross-configuration learning and manufacturability/reliability/uncertainty terms for wide-bandgap power modules in high-efficiency energy systems (Chen, quoted on combining geometry-informed AI with advanced multiphysics modeling toward "more efficient, reliable and manufacturable power electronics"). **Two subawards**: **Nengkun Yu** (professor, Department of Computer Science), *Neuro-Symbolic Synthesis of Verified Computational Physics Code for Scientific Discovery*, led by **Johns Hopkins University** (**Stony Brook Awarded $99,999**) — AI code generation plus symbolic reasoning that verifies mathematical and physical requirements, for faster and more reliable scientific software on high-performance and quantum computing systems; **Anatoly Frenkel** (professor, Materials Science and Chemical Engineering), *Transient Kinetics and Spectroscopy for Agentic Digital Twins to Upgrade Domestic Alkane Feedstocks into Value-Added Chemicals*, received **through Brookhaven National Laboratory** with **The Pennsylvania State University**, **Georgia Institute of Technology** and **ExxonMobil Corporation** (**Total amount to the team: $750,000**) — an AI-enabled "digital twin" framework for catalysts converting domestic alkane feedstocks such as propane into higher-value chemicals, combining rapid transient reactor measurements with infrared, Raman and X-ray absorption spectroscopy, with the Frenkel group contributing advanced **operando** X-ray spectroscopy and machine-learning-assisted analysis of catalyst restructuring under working conditions and targeting catalyst evaluation **up to 20 times faster** than conventional methods while keeping accurate activity and selectivity predictions. **Institutional mobilization (independent corroboration)**: the awards follow a coordinated university-wide effort producing **89 Stony Brook submissions** — **40** university-led across **16 research areas** (AI, advanced computing, physics, microelectronics, energy systems, materials science, interdisciplinary research) and **49** with Stony Brook as collaborating institution. **Quoted**: President **Andrea Goldsmith** ("validates our position as a national leader in expanding the scope, scale and impact of research in science and engineering by leveraging the powerful tool of AI"; ## [3.34.31] - 2026-10-08

### Added
- **Processed new reference**: [NSF 26-512: Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets) — Program Solicitation](https://www.nsf.gov/funding/opportunities/ai-datasets-unlocking-dataset-value-ai-enabled-scientific-discovery/nsf26-512/solicitation) — the **Program Solicitation** document of the U.S. **National Science Foundation** funding opportunity **NSF 26-512** (host domain `www.nsf.gov`, page title *NSF 26-512: Unlocking Dataset Value for AI-Enabled Scientific Discovery (AI Datasets) | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation*, active funding opportunity served as "the current version", solicitation **Document History: Posted July 21, 2026**), fetched and verified in this round. Distinct from the already-indexed *AI Datasets* opportunity landing page, this is the solicitation instrument itself. **Issuing structure**: a cross-directorate program run jointly by the NSF **Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE)**, **Directorate for Biological Sciences**, **Directorate for Engineering**, **Directorate for Geosciences**, **Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences** and **Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP)** together with the **Office of Research Infrastructure**; program contact `aidatasets@nsf.gov`; Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance numbers **47.041, 47.049, 47.050, 47.070, 47.074, 47.084**. **Programme goal**: increase the value derivable from *existing* scientific datasets via (1) AI-based **feature extraction, metadata generation and integration of multiple datasets**, (2) **robust data pipelines** for automated analysis, and (3) **augmentation and harmonization** of existing datasets for AI data pipelines — with the solicitation's stated diagnosis that many scientific datasets are not findable, accessible or interoperable and lack the integrity, data descriptors and pipelines needed by large-scale AI applications, that AI systems increasingly become *the initial consumer* of datasets, and that many datasets lack identified owners or sufficiently organized scientific communities; research to collect **de novo** datasets is expressly **out of scope** and stays with the individual scientific directorates. **Award structure**: anticipated funding **$60,000,000–$100,000,000** (subject to the availability of funds) across an estimated **25 to 50 awards** as standard grants or cooperative agreements — **Impact awards** up to 3 years / maximum **$2,000,000** (approx. 10–20), **Flagship awards** up to 3 years / maximum **$5,000,000** (approx. 5–10, for "more complex challenges that are not achievable without more substantial resources"), and **Planning grants** up to **$200,000** (approx. 10–20); **Full Proposal deadline November 04, 2026** and the **first Wednesday in November, annually thereafter**, 5 p.m. submitting-organization local time; no letters of intent or preliminary proposals; **voluntary committed cost sharing prohibited**; no PI or proposal-count limits; single lead organization with subawards; active **UEI through SAM.gov** required. **Genesis Mission coupling**: aligned with the **America's AI Action Plan** (world-class AI-ready scientific datasets and public release of high-quality datasets from prior federally funded research named as priorities) and supporting the **Genesis Mission**, described as an effort "to build an integrated platform to harness scientific datasets to train scientific models, create AI agents to test new hypotheses, automate research workflows and accelerate scientific breakthroughs"; proposals are encouraged to leverage **NSF data platforms**, the **NSF Integrated Data Systems and Services (IDSS)** program, the **NSF-led National AI Research Resource (NAIRR)**, the **Genesis Mission platform** or other national infrastructure, and NSF is open to **philanthropy, private industry and non-profit partnerships**. **Mandatory content & review**: dataset **governance** (access, retirement policies, community contribution process) and **security and integrity** (provenance, trust, quality, privacy, authenticity, sensitive datasets, research-security issues); Project Description sections *Vision and community benefit for dataset enhancement*, *Research plan*, *Dataset governance and integrity*, *Dataset availability and infrastructure* plus a **Flagship Justification**; title prefixes **"AIDatasets:Impact"**, **"AIDatasets:Flagship"**, **"AIDatasets:Planning"** and a `Keywords:` line of 2–5 keywords; National Science Board **Intellectual Merit**/**Broader Impacts** plus five solicitation-specific criteria (community size/commitment/impact/breadth/outreach, novelty and transformative potential, security-integrity-governance with sustainment, adoption viability and ease, Flagship funding justification) under **panel review** after a compliance check, an NSF Program Officer review and three or more external experts. Citing **Executive Order 14332** (*Improving Oversight of Federal Grantmaking*), NSF **may give preference to institutions with lower indirect cost rates** all else being equal after merit review, and awards may include **termination for convenience** provisions. **Eligibility**: two- and four-year IHEs including community colleges, non-profit non-academic organizations (museums, observatories, research laboratories, professional societies), U.S.-based for-profits including small businesses, State and Local Governments, **Tribal Nations** (25 U.S.C. §§ 5130–5131), and other Federal Agencies and **FFRDCs** (PAPPG Chapter I.E.2). **Measures of success**: datasets expanded or established and new AI techniques/AI-guided exploration; **undergraduates and graduate students trained in the AI use of scientific datasets**; new built infrastructure leveraging existing datasets and research facility usage; awardees commit to **bi-annual virtual meetings** and budgeted in-person meetings including the **NSF NAIRR community meeting**.
- **Enriched paper sections**: `README.md` §3.4 *Federal Agencies & Policy Bodies* — the **National Science Foundation (NSF)** profile received a new **AI Datasets Program Solicitation (NSF 26-512)** sub-entry with five sub-bullets (*Award structure & schedule*, *Technical scope*, *Genesis Mission coupling*, *Governance, eligibility & review requirements*, *Measures of success & community obligations*) covering the three award tiers and their ceilings, the 4 November 2026 and first-Wednesday-in-November deadlines, the cost-sharing/UEI/lead-organization rules, the feature-extraction → data-pipeline → harmonization scope with the de-novo-collection exclusion and legacy-dataset-readiness platforms, the America's AI Action Plan and Genesis Mission "integrated platform … train scientific models … create AI agents to test new hypotheses" framing, the IDSS/NAIRR/NSF-data-platform leverage expectation and philanthropy/industry/non-profit partnership opening, the governance/security/integrity requirements, the "AIDatasets:…" title prefixes, the full eligibility ladder from community colleges to Tribal Nations and FFRDCs, the five additional merit-review criteria, the **EO 14332** lower-indirect-cost-rate preference and termination-for-convenience note, and the success measures including student training and the NAIRR community meeting; Appendix **A.1** received a new **NSF AI Datasets Program (NSF 26-512)** row. Developing complex scientific applications large enough to run on them is another." Discovery is recorded as "a key component in ORNL’s work on the DOE Genesis Mission", continuing to advance AI-enabled high-performance modeling and simulation and exploring potential computing paradigms at the **convergence of HPC, AI and quantum computing**, with the Genesis Mission described as DOE's endeavor to build "the world’s most powerful scientific platform to accelerate discovery science, strengthen national security, and drive energy innovation". **Evaluation criteria**: potential for scientific advancements, usefulness to the broader scientific community, and contribution to programming models, algorithms, AI and other innovations. **Two key requirements**: submitting an acceleration plan demonstrating **at least a fivefold performance improvement** over applications currently running on **Frontier** and similar exascale systems, and instantiating a compelling **challenge problem** to be performed on Discovery. **Support package for accepted projects**: early access to Discovery, special training sessions and hackathons, direct OLCF staff assistance for **code porting, profiling and optimization**, support from staff at **AMD** and **Hewlett Packard Enterprises** via the **ORNL HPE/AMD Center of Excellence**, and compute-time allocations on **Frontier** and other early hardware resources. **Named people and quotes**: **Arjun Shankar** (director of the OLCF and of the National Center for Computational Sciences at ORNL) on Discovery continuing "ORNL’s and DOE’s proven record of HPC leadership" while supporting "the Genesis Mission’s scientific productivity goals"; **Reuben Budiardja** (CAAR program lead and ORNL group leader for Advanced Computing for Nuclear, Particle and Astrophysics) on the goal of running applications "on day one", on CAAR as "an ideal venue for exploring different computational techniques, for example, the pros and cons of using lower precision and mixed precision calculations", and on broadening HPC/AI availability by inviting teams from all areas of science and all levels of computing experience — including applications that "have had issues with GPU-acceleration and scalability" — with Discovery's problems spanning "from drug discovery to nuclear fuels and the origins of the universe"; Physicist and professor **Stephanie Majewski** — joined by collaborators at **Brown University** and **Brookhaven National Laboratory** — leads **MANGO**, an abbreviation for ***Monte Carlo Acceleration via Normalizing Flows using GPU Optimization***, which uses AI to save time and computing costs for experiments at CERN's **Large Hadron Collider (LHC)** by re-thinking **Monte Carlo event generation**: the release names it "a bottleneck standing between raw collider data and physics discovery" (**each collision at the LHC produces terabytes of raw data**), and MANGO re-thinks the entire generation process to produce simulations that are **both dramatically faster and more accurate**, "a combination that hasn't existed before". Hardware strategy as stated: the optimization can be implemented in computing farms using both **GPUs and CPUs** and **doesn't require special hardware**, with a main goal of being applicable to different types of hardware and therefore **independent of a particular GPU brand** (**NVIDIA** and **AMD** named as manufacturers), potentially helping experiments at CERN and the work of particle theorists. Lead background recorded from the release: ATLAS experiment member at CERN since **2007**, UO professor of physics since **2012**, member of the UO **Institute for Fundamental Science**, and currently **deputy project manager** for the upgrade preparing CERN's detectors for the **High Luminosity LHC** accelerator upgrade ("What is dark matter?"). Quoted on the Genesis Mission's AI-driven scientific-computing investment translating "directly into faster, cheaper insight" from LHC datasets, on how efficiently "the country's multi-billion-dollar investment in fundamental science gets turned into discovery", on "every dollar we save on computing" advancing new physics and U.S. leadership, and on training "the next generation of scientists at the intersection of AI and physics" for skills the broader economy needs.

## [1.0.0] - 2026-08-08

### Initial Major Release — The Genesis Mission Reference Architecture

The **v1.0.0** release establishes the definitive, open-source technical reference paper and ecosystem topology index for the **Genesis Mission**: a multi-billion-dollar federal initiative coupling Artificial Intelligence (AI), fault-tolerant quantum computing, and exascale high-performance computing (HPC).

### Key Highlights
- **100% Ecosystem Coverage (148 Core Flagship Nodes)**:
  - **17 DOE National Laboratories**: Complete technical profile for ANL, BNL, INL, LBNL, LLNL, LANL, NETL, NREL, ORNL, PNNL, PPPL, SNL, SRNL, SLAC, TJNAF, Fermilab, and Ames.
  - **61 Industry & Hyperscale Partners**: Architectural integration covering AWS, Google DeepMind, Microsoft, NVIDIA, AMD, Dell Technologies, HPE, IBM Quantum, SambaNova Systems, Cerebras, Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta AI, Scale AI, Hugging Face, FutureHouse, LILA, Applied Materials, Synopsys, Siemens, xLight, and key critical materials/energy partners.
  - **9 Federal Agencies & Executive Bodies**: Governance overview spanning White House OSTP, DOE Office of Science, DOC NIST/CHIPS R&D Office, NSF, NIH/HHS, NASA, DOD (Department of War), DHS S&T, and DOI.
  - **4 Specialized Research & Healthcare Hubs**: Profiles for Cleveland Clinic, Johns Hopkins University APL, AI Tennessee Initiative, and RTI International.
  - **57 Awardee Research Universities**: Categorized academic nodes across quantum science, AI/SciML, materials discovery, nuclear physics, and grid decarbonization.
- **Three Core Technical Pillars**:
  1. *Heterogeneous HPC Substrate*: Exascale supercomputers (*Frontier*, *Aurora*, *El Capitan*, *Solstice*, *Equinox*, *Lux*, *Discovery*), Dell AI Factory, and SambaNova Reconfigurable Dataflow RDUs.
  2. *Quantum Leadership & CHIPS Act Foundries*: Over $2B in DOE quantum leadership programs matched by $2B+ Commerce CHIPS Act LOIs spanning 7 modalities (superconducting, trapped-ion, neutral-atom, photonic, silicon spin, and cross-modality foundries).
  3. *Closed-Loop Agentic Scientific Workflows*: Autonomous AI agents orchestrating quantum-classical algorithms, robotic wet labs, and real-time sensor streams (synchrotrons, tokamaks, accelerators).
- **Strategic Capital Mechanics**: Detailed allocation architecture tracking >$3.5 Billion across FOA grants, national security challenges, CHIPS Act incentives, and hyperscaler compute credits.
- **Curated Reference Index**: Comprehensive external citation index in `references.md` mapping federal releases, FOA solicitations, lab disclosures, and corporate announcements.
